mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium as investors anticipate future rate hikes, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in a given month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 5-day rolling average by more than one standard deviation, or inflation reverts below 0.3% within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS labor cost index above prior month's value signals wage pressure, prompting equity market anticipation of higher profits and a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > PAYEMS[lag1] for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes where unemployment < 5%, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05), or wage growth reverses direction within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST retail sales accompanied by a decline in RSAFS industrial supply index indicates strengthening consumer demand, which predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > HOUST[lag1] and RSAFS < RSAFS[lag1] in the same month
failure_condition: Across 10 such events, the average 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the effect is explained by at least two other macro variables with higher R-squared.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in INDPRO manufacturing index below 95 suggests supply-side constraints, elevating risk premia and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In 10 such episodes, the 5-day forward returns do not average below zero (p > 0.05), or the effect is absent when other supply indicators (e.g., Durable Goods Orders) show no similar pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in FEDFUNDS rates without a corresponding rise in CPIAUCSL inflation predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as discount rates are expected to remain lower.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS declines for 3 consecutive months and CPIAUCSL remains below 0.2% over the same period
failure_condition: Over 15 such episodes, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the effect persists only when other rate surprises are absent.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in UNRATE unemployment rate above 5.5% in a month leads to a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates slower growth and tighter credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.5% in a single month
failure_condition: Across 8 such events, the 60-day forward returns do not average below zero (p > 0.05), or the effect is absent when other labor indicators (e.g., PAYEMS) show no similar trend.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly increases in GDPC1 personal consumption and HOUST retail sales, with no offsetting decline in RSAFS, signal robust demand growth and a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > GDPC1[lag1] and HOUST > HOUST[lag1] and RSAFS < RSAFS[lag1]
failure_condition: The interaction R-squared is < 0.5 when regressing 20-day forward returns on the three proxies, or the effect is not significant in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in INDPRO accompanied by a rise in RSAFS supply index (both above their prior month) indicates easing supply constraints and a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO[lag1] and RSAFS > RSAFS[lag1] for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 12 such events, the 60-day forward returns do not beat the 5-day baseline by more than one standard deviation, or the effect is driven by other supply or demand variables with higher explanatory power.
